title: ASR Controlled Vocabularies
description: Single source of truth for every closed enum in the Authoritative Source Registry standard. Object schemas $ref these definitions (e.g. "vocab.json#/$defs/verification_state") so terminology is defined in exactly one place. Extensible fields anyOf a closed enum with an "x-" prefixed escape hatch; validators report x- values as advisory x_extension warnings so non-standard vocabulary stays visible.

source_role.description: What the source IS structurally. A publisher originates content; an aggregator or index points at content held elsewhere (its entries are pointers — agents should follow them to the underlying primary documents rather than citing the aggregator as the authority); a repository or archive holds deposited/preserved materials; a mirror re-serves another source; a community source is collectively authored.

source_class.description: Evidential distance from the facts. primary: the source of record (the statute itself, the agency's own program page, the dataset produced by the measuring organization). secondary: credible analysis or reporting about primary material. tertiary: orientation and discovery layers (aggregators, encyclopedic summaries of summaries).

authority_tier.description: Three-tier triage of source authority, carried in-band with this legend. 1 = primary/authoritative: statute or regulation text, court opinions, government agency or national-laboratory publications, standards bodies, primary datasets. 2 = credible secondary: established NGOs and think tanks, trade press with editorial standards, academic-adjacent trackers, professional organizations. 3 = orientation only: aggregator listings, advocacy material, commercial teasers, manufacturer PR. Tier is a triage judgment, not a score; see the authority block's asserted/adjudicated split.

authority_basis.description: WHY a source is authoritative — the grounds for trust. Multiple bases may apply (an agency page describing its own statute-mandated program is government_agency + regulation).

access_type.description: The transport shape of one way into a source. api_rest / api_graphql: structured request-response APIs. oai_pmh: OAI-PMH metadata harvesting. feed: RSS/Atom. bulk_download: whole files or datasets fetched by URL. web_fetch: plain HTTP pages readable without JavaScript. web_render: pages requiring JavaScript rendering — the transport claim is verifiable by plain HTTP, but content extraction is delegated to a rendering harness. ftp: FTP/SFTP. offline: material that must be obtained out of band (recorded for completeness; never probed).

auth_scheme.description: How an access method authenticates. Values name the mechanism AND where the secret travels: api_key_query (key as a query parameter), api_key_header (key in a named header), bearer_token (Authorization: Bearer), http_basic, oauth2 (recorded for completeness; token acquisition is out of scope for the reference CLI), session_cookie (recorded so the blocked/login_required state is explainable — NEVER automated). none = open access. Profiles never store secret values, only a credential_ref (§05).

verification_state.description: The lifecycle state of an access claim — the vocabulary of the hard promise. verified: the last probe succeeded, its evidence hashes match, and it is within the staleness window. stale: was verified, but the window has lapsed; re-probe to restore. asserted: recorded from documentation or discovery, never successfully probed — an honest 'I have not actually tried this'. degraded: probe succeeded but with warning signs (slow, partial, deprecation headers). broken: the last probe failed for a non-blocking reason (timeout, DNS, 5xx). blocked: the source refused (403, robots disallow, paywall, login wall) — a recorded terminal state, not a challenge to overcome. retired: manually closed (source defunct or method withdrawn). States are DERIVED from probe records by the rules in §04; a stored state that disagrees with derivation is flagged state_drift.

probe_outcome.description: Terminal outcome of one probe execution. ok: all checks passed. degraded: reachable with warning signs. failed: network or server failure (retryable class: timeout, dns_error, tls_error recorded separately for diagnosis). blocked: refused with an auth-independent 4xx. robots_disallowed: robots.txt disallows the probed path — no request was made past the robots check. auth_required: a credential was needed and did not resolve — the claim stays asserted, never an error. auth_invalid: a credential resolved but was rejected (401/403 with credential present). moved: permanent redirect off the profiled base URL — the profile needs updating.

probe_check.description: One verification step inside a probe. robots: robots.txt fetched and parsed for the probed path. http: transport-level request (HEAD or bounded GET). api_parse: response parsed as the endpoint's declared response format. auth: credential resolution and acceptance. render: full-render verification — only a rendering harness can pass this; the reference CLI records it as skip for web_render methods.

check_result.description: Result of one probe check. skip means the check did not apply or could not run (e.g. render in a non-rendering CLI, auth when no credential resolves) — skips are visible, never silently dropped.

fetch_status.description: Acquisition outcome of a fetch, verbatim from UPC's retrieval vocabulary so ASR fetch sidecars map onto UPC sources field-for-field (crosswalks/upc.md).

artifact_kind.description: What kind of content object a source holds (the content model — deliberately separate from HOW it is accessed). structured_record means individually addressable records (an API result, a database row, a catalog entry) as opposed to a dataset_file downloaded whole.

landing_pattern.description: How many hops from the public URL to the artifact you actually want. direct: the URL is the artifact. landing_then_file: a landing page fronts the real file (the 'report landing page' pattern — agents should follow the file link, not extract the landing page). landing_then_viewer: a landing page opens an embedded viewer; the underlying file needs a distinct URL. search_then_record: records are reached through a search or docket interface. portal_query: a query portal must be driven to produce the artifact (export builders, data explorers).

lifecycle_status.description: Whether the source itself is a going concern. active: maintained and updating. dormant: not updating but intact and expected to return. archived: frozen intentionally, content stable and citable. deprecated: publisher points users elsewhere. defunct: gone or abandoned; profile retained for the historical record.

update_cadence.description: How often the source's CONTENT changes (distinct from access-method stability — a static archive is reachable daily but never updates). continuous: rolling updates without a schedule (live program pages, dockets 'updated as filed'). static: complete and final. unknown is honest and allowed.

jurisdiction_level.description: Granularity of the governing or covering jurisdiction. Pair with regions[] (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or 3166-2 codes, e.g. "US", "US-CA") for the specific places. A federal court ruling scoped to one state is national level with a subnational region plus notes.

relation_type.description: Typed edge between sources. aggregates: this source indexes/points at the target's material. api_for: this source is the programmatic face of the target (e.g. a data API for an agency). part_of: organizational containment (a lab within a department). supersedes / superseded_by: succession, including domain moves (a moved homepage is a NEW source related by supersedes — ids are stable). companion_of: sibling services commonly used together.

pagination_style.description: How an endpoint pages through results. page_number: a page parameter. offset_limit: offset/limit or start/rows. cursor: an opaque cursor returned in each response. token: a continuation token (OAI-PMH resumptionToken). link_header: RFC 5988 Link rel="next".

robots_posture.description: What robots.txt says about the access method's base path, as captured at probe time. partial: some relevant paths disallowed. no_robots: no robots.txt served (fetch returned 404/empty) — treated as allowed but recorded distinctly. not_applicable: robots does not govern this transport (authenticated APIs, ftp, offline).

response_format.description: Declared wire format of an endpoint's response, checked by the api_parse probe. binary covers anything opaque; zip covers packaged downloads.

evidence_kind.description: What a stored probe-evidence file is. robots_txt: the full robots.txt bytes as served. headers: the response status line and headers subset, serialized as JSON. body_sample: leading bytes of a response body, truncated at a recorded byte count, with the full body's hash recorded alongside when known.

credential_source.description: Which step of the resolution chain produced a credential (recorded in probe/fetch records so runs are explainable; the VALUE is never recorded). env: AUTHORITY_CRED_<REF>. env_forge: FORGE_API_KEY_<REF> (pi-forge compatibility). file: the registry's gitignored credentials.json. keychain: macOS Keychain via security(1). none: nothing resolved.

auth_location.description: Where an api_key style secret travels: query = a named query parameter, header = a named HTTP header.

http_method.description: HTTP methods an endpoint recipe may declare. HEAD appears only in probe records; endpoints declare GET or POST.

confidence.description: Qualitative confidence, shared vocabulary with UPC (used in guidance and discovery annotations).

produced_by_method.description: How an object came to be written. human: typed by a person. model: authored by an LLM (adjudication blocks with method=model draw the adjudication_by_machine warning — machine judgment must not masquerade as human judgment). tool: computed mechanically (probe records, regen outputs). import: converted from an external corpus or manifest. fixture: written by a deterministic example/test builder — fixtures never lie, but they say what they are.
